decisions.thought: Mirror match: the opponent's team is an exact copy of mine. Plan: Incineroar leads to Fake Out and Intimidate, then Garchomp (Mega) and Gholdengo do the damage. Expect the opponent to bring its own Incineroar, Garchomp and Gholdengo or a similar mix. Watch for Dragapult's speed and possible Infiltrator.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Against a mirror team I'm leaning toward Incineroar as lead for Fake Out and Intimidate, pairing with Mega Garchomp as a core threat, and considering Gholdengo for special coverage.

decisions.thought: Opponent's Corviknight has Mirror Armor, so my Attack drops reflect back at me. Incineroar's Intimidate was reflected and cut my own Attack. Fake Out is weak here (Normal is resisted by Steel). Flare Blitz is super effective on Corviknight. Plan: pressure Corviknight with Flare Blitz, then bring in Garchomp or Gholdengo for the rest. Opponent team mirrors mine: expect Dragapult (speed threat), Gholdengo, Garchomp, Sinistcha. Avoid switching Garchomp in where Stone Edge or Earthquake gets blunted.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Against Corviknight's Mirror Armor, Fake Out is only half-effective since Normal is resisted by Steel, but it still hits for 40 power with a flinch chance. Flare Blitz is the better option here, landing as a 120-power super-effective Fire move against Corviknight's Flying/Steel typing.

decisions.thought: Turn 2: Dragapult (72%, faster than Incineroar) resists my Fire attack, so Flare Blitz is poor. Plan: Parting Shot to cut its Atk and SpA and bring in Gholdengo, whose Shadow Ball is super effective on Dragapult. Corviknight (Mirror Armor, U-turn) is in the back. Garchomp (Garchompite) is the Mega threat for later. Opponent may still bring Garchomp, Gholdengo or Sinistcha.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 159/202 with Atk -1, facing an active Dragapult at 72% and Corviknight having switched out after U-turn. Since Dragapult outspeeds and resists Fire as a Dragon-type, Flare Blitz won't do much, so I'm weighing whether Dark-type coverage is better against it given Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing.

I'm considering Parting Shot to debuff Dragapult and pivot into Garchomp or Gholdengo, thinking through whether either handles Dragapult's Dragon/Ghost typing well and whether Mega Garchomp's speed tier helps here.

Ghost isn't super effective against Steel, so Gholdengo should be fine there. Parting Shot drops Dragapult's Atk and SpA while letting me pivot Incineroar out, so I'll use that and bring in Gholdengo on the switch.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to decide between switching to Garchomp or Gholdengo here, with Incineroar active and Dragapult at 72% in the back. If I go Mega Garchomp, it's Dragon/Ground with Sand Force rather than Rough Skin, which changes the calculus.

Gholdengo as Steel/Ghost resists Fire but takes double from Dark, so Incineroar's likely Knock Off is a real threat. Still, Gholdengo's Make It Rain or Thunderbolt could hit Incineroar hard given its SpA, so I'm weighing whether that trade favors us against Incineroar's Def/SpD bulk.

Garchomp's Earthquake looks cleaner against Incineroar, hitting neutrally with huge power and outspeeding it, which sets up Mega Garchomp pressure for later turns. But I also need to factor in Dragapult, since its Ghost-type attacks hit Gholdengo for double damage, complicating which mon should lead against that threat.

I'll go with Garchomp: it's fast, Mega is available next turn, and Dragon/Ground takes Fire neutrally and Dark neutrally too.

Dragapult's wide speed range (145-213) could outpace Garchomp's 158, so there's a real chance it moves first, but Dragon Claw at 2x should still do massive damage or secure the KO. I'll go with Dragon Claw.

Stone Edge is the better call here — solid damage now despite 80% accuracy, keeps Gholdengo fresh for later, and avoids giving Corviknight a free Roost turn while it's switched in.
